### Here's how to self-host it
[Permalink: Here's how to self-host it](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain#heres-how-to-self-host-it)

GBrain is MIT-licensed and free to self-host. It needs **Bun 1.4.4 or newer**; existing worker installs read the [authorization and queue upgrade guide](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/guides/authorization-upgrade.md) before restarting on this version.

Warning

**GBrain is NOT distributed on npm.** The npm `gbrain` package is unrelated and can shadow the real binary, so never run `npm install -g gbrain` or `bun add -g gbrain`. Install only via `bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable` (the soaked stable channel; `#latest-stable` is the alpha line with every release) or `git clone --branch stable` + `bun install && bun link`. Installed by mistake? `gbrain doctor` gives the fix. Schema not migrated ( [#218](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/issues/218))? Run `gbrain apply-migrations --yes --no-autopilot-install`; if it exits 1, run `gbrain doctor --json`, not another `--yes` (`wedged`: relay its fix).

```
bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable
gbrain setup claude-code              # or: gbrain setup codex
gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding   # any other harness, or no agent
```

### Add your notes and your company's docs
Then open a new agent session and ask _"What did we decide about a free plan, and why?"_: the answer comes from your decisions log. `--federated` puts the folder in default search, and `--force` accepts a folder that isn't a git repository; in a folder that is one, GBrain reads only committed files, so commit your edits before you sync. To see the shape first, `gbrain sources demo company-brain` runs a fictional company in a few seconds without touching your brain. Before you share a company brain with a team, read the [company-brain tutorial](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/tutorials/company-brain.md).

GBrain is not a data warehouse or analytics store. Keep ads, analytics, CRM and payment data in your warehouse, and connect your agent to it separately.

### Connect GBrain to your AI client (MCP)
- **Local stdio client:**`gbrain setup claude-code` or `gbrain setup codex` registers `gbrain serve` (lists the memory verbs; `--surface full` lists every tool) behind gbrain's launcher, so a session opened in a cloned repository never loads that repository's `bunfig.toml` or `.env`, and adds the brain-first instructions: agents seldom call a brain nobody told them about. Cursor, Windsurf and other stdio clients take `"$(command -v gbrain)" serve --surface starter --advertise verbs`.
- **Plugins with curated skills:** Codex `codex plugin marketplace add garrytan/gbrain@codex-plugin` + `codex plugin add gbrain@gbrain`; Claude Code `/plugin marketplace add garrytan/gbrain` + `/plugin install gbrain@gbrain`.
- **This brain from anywhere:**`gbrain mcp expose` publishes it on your Tailscale tailnet as a user service (`--funnel` for cloud agents such as Grok Bot, Muse and ChatGPT). [Guide](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/guides/remote-mcp.md).
- **A brain on another host:**`gbrain connect https://your-host/mcp --token gbrain_xxx --install` (add `--agent codex` for Codex). Hosted brains use [native OAuth or a private handoff](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/guides/hosted-harness-access.md); dashboard, clients and permissions live in [MCP administration](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/mcp/ADMIN.md).

        "description": "Stability: which gbrain you get and how it changes

gbrain ships new releases many times a day. Most people should not run every one of them, and by default they don't: a normal install follows the stable channel, which only moves to a release after it has passed extra testing. This page says what that means in practice and how to choose something slower or faster.

What the default install gives you

The install command in the README, bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable, installs the current stable release. git clone --branch stable does the same. A new brain created by gbrain init (no earlier config file) is set to the stable channel, and an install with no channel set follows stable too. Every update path follows the channel in effect: the update notice, gbrain check-update, gbrain upgrade, gbrain self-upgrade and the opt-in automatic upgrades.
Check which channel you are on with gbrain doctor, which prints channel=<channel> when one is set.

How a release becomes stable

1. Every release passes the full test suite first. A release is published only after the full unit and end-to-end test runs pass on its exact code.
2. A stable candidate then passes a production-shaped test. gbrain runs a two-hour load test on a brain of 600,000 pages, at two network delays (2 ms and 65 ms), with privacy probes. It must pass the privacy-leak, read-error, version-skew, process-health and session checks in every run. The test has to have run on the release's exact files; a test of a nearby commit doesn't count.
3. Stable moves only for a reason. A scheduled check runs twice a day (05:17 and 13:17 UTC). It promotes the newest release that passed step 2, and only when there is a reason to move:
* an important fix (a security, regression or data-loss fix, or a fix for something that blocks people) has been released but is not in stable yet, or

...

Between then and 15 November 2026 stable moved 9 more times: once on 6 November, 9.7 days later, and then on each of the 8 days from 8 to 15 November, because an important fix was waiting on each of those days. Each move carried every change released since the one before. To see the current pace, list every stable release:
git ls-remote --tags --refs github.com/garrytan/gbrain 'refs/tags/stable-v*'

Staying on stable

Do nothing; it is the default. To set it explicitly, or to come back to it from the fast channel:
gbrain config set self_upgrade.channel stable
gbrain upgrade --dry-run --json   # what an upgrade would install, installing nothing
gbrain never downgrades you by itself. If you ran ahead on the fast channel and switch back, you stay on your release until stable passes it. The one exception is a release that was withdrawn (listed as known_bad in the stable record): an install on it is offered the current stable release, even when that is older.
Updates are not applied by themselves unless you opt in. The default self_upgrade.mode is notify: you are told an update exists and nothing is installed without your say-so.

Pinning a version

Install an exact release tag with this command. Its first line checks that the tag exists. Its second line removes any gbrain Bun already has installed, because installing one tag over another can leave the old version running and damage Bun's global package list. Its third line installs the tag:
git ls-remote --exit-code --tags github.com/garrytan/gbrain refs/tags/v<version> >/dev/null && \
  { ! bun pm ls -g 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'gbrain@' || bun remove -g gbrain; } && \
  bun add -g --backend=copyfile github:garrytan/gbrain#v<version>
